newsitem.title: UK: EU grains crumble under supplies, lower Chicago.
newsitem.headline: EU grains crumble under supplies, lower Chicago.

text.p: European grains drifted lower on their path towards intervention levels this week with tumbling U.S. futures putting extra pressure on prices, traders said.
The complete absence of the sort of demand that can match supply forced benchmark prices down for most of Europe, except Spain where farmers held grain to create artificial strength.
The pressure was exacerbated by French grain cooperatives which actively sold in anticipation prices may drop further.
But at mid-week, attention again turned to the European Union's (EU) tender on Thursday with traders curious to see if the EU will prop up its refund to cover fragile wheat exports.
Brussel's move this week is key for French exporters, eager to cover their sale of 150,000 tonnes of soft wheat to Egypt.
Last week, the EU stepped up its subsidy on wheat to 19.98 Ecus per tonne amid a sharp fall in world prices. The sale valued French wheat for late November at some $150 per tonne.
But the EU carefully avoided covering the sale to Egypt clinched at $146.50-$147, Fob, as this would have meant undercutting U.S. prices and sparking a new subsidy war.
Traders estimated a refund of 23-24 Ecus to cover that sale.
New contract lows below $4.00 a bushel were set in Chicago wheat futures this week after an impressive rating for the U.S. winter wheat crop.
French delivered grain prices dropped sharply this week with November wheat into Roeuen trading at 830 francs, down from 855.
The German wheat market was also depressed by supply pressure from other European origins and overseas.

"There is very little demand for any quality. Consumers here are looking to France and southern Europe is buying from North America," one broker said. "Prices will have to ease further, especially premiums for quality wheat."
UK delivered prices were pummelled by sterling which galloped to new highs against the dollar. Spot feed wheat sank below the 100 stg mark and is even cheaper than feed barley.
"Sterling is a big factor but farmers are also selling," said one trader.
EU barley was generally in doldrums due to a lack of export prospects but traders were expected to put further pressure on the Commission this week for substantial refunds and tonnages.
Maize collection in France has gained momentum after a delay in September. This was creating backlog in some silos, turning grain cooperatives into sellers, French traders said.
Prices were under pressure. French maize dropped 25 francs over the week, while in Spain they eased on reports that harvest quality was good with 15 percent completed in the north.

Spain's ex-farm feed wheat prices climbed slightly with co-operatives tending to hold back supplies. Standard milling wheat was steady, although high quality milling wheat rose slightly with buyers awarding a premium for the good quality.
Spain was receiving enquiries from Greece and Italy for its high quality durum this year -- a factor underpinning prices. But farmers were selling more barley, pressuring prices.
Italian wheat headed south while durum wheat was stable under 300,000 lire. Traders said prices were bottoming out.
"Both wheat and maize prices seem to have bottomed out and should stay at the current levels or rise slightly", one dealer said noting that demand usually picks up before Christmas.
